name: Endpoint Denial of Service
description:
Adversaries may perform Endpoint Denial of Service (DoS) attacks to degrade or block the availability of services to users.

On Android versions prior to 7, apps can abuse Device Administrator access to reset the device lock passcode, preventing the user from unlocking the device. After Android 7, only device or profile owners (e.g. MDMs) can reset the device’s passcode.(Citation: Android resetPassword)

On iOS devices, this technique does not work because mobile device management servers can only remove the screen lock passcode; they cannot set a new passcode. However, on jailbroken devices, malware has been discovered that can lock the user out of the device.(Citation: Xiao-KeyRaider)

references.description: Claud Xiao. (2015, August 30). KeyRaider: iOS Malware Steals Over 225,000 Apple Accounts to Create Free App Utopia. Retrieved December 12, 2016.

telemetry.name: API Calls
telemetry.description: Instrumented mobile API calls and results relevant to an application behavior.
telemetry.collection_focus: Instrument selected APIs in the owned test app or approved research build; log caller, API, sanitized argument class and return status.

providers.name: Android logcat
providers.scope: Permitted logs from a consented test device/emulator; output depends on build, permissions and instrumentation.

providers.name: Android dumpsys
providers.scope: Point-in-time service/package state on an authorized development device.

providers.name: Instrumented test application
providers.scope: Own-app permission, API and state callbacks; not universal visibility into other apps.

configuration: Use a disposable emulator or owned development device with approved debugging. Record OS/API level, app version and instrumentation privileges.
Collect only relevant logcat buffers/tags and service snapshots; add explicit own-app instrumentation for events absent from OS logs.
Forward sanitized logs and compare before/after state. Remove test data and revoke debugging access after the lab session.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Android tooling does not imply iOS coverage. Standard mobile apps cannot observe all other apps or protected OS internals; MDM status is not full API, filesystem or content telemetry.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Per owned device, app version and permission state: unexpected API/permission changes, background activity and network destinations. OS privacy restrictions and emulator differences limit observability.

telemetry.name: Host Status
telemetry.description: Host health and availability observations such as heartbeat, shutdown or degraded state.
telemetry.collection_focus: Collect agent heartbeat and OS health independently; record missed polls, last-seen time and monitor health.

providers.name: osquery
providers.scope: Scheduled host-state queries; supported tables and privileges vary by OS. Select a table that actually exposes the required object.

providers.name: Linux Audit plus inventory snapshots
providers.scope: Events explain changes; snapshots describe state at collection time.

configuration: Define the inventory query, allowed host set, interval and least-privileged reader. Store a stable asset ID, observation time and collector version.
Keep successive snapshots and calculate additions, removals and changed attributes. Pair state changes with audit events when available.
Export collector health and missed-poll counts so a missing snapshot is not misclassified as a missing asset.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Snapshots miss short-lived objects and do not identify who caused a change. A generic inventory agent is not guaranteed to expose firmware or kernel-level details.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Compare authorized state snapshots: first-seen drivers/services/modules, unexpected configuration drift and integrity changes. Record collection cadence; absence in a sample is not evidence of deletion.

strategies.name: Detection of Endpoint Denial of Service

analytics.name: Analytic 1695
analytics.guidance: For Android, detect Endpoint Denial of Service by correlating analyst-visible device/network evidence and management state; use streaming or batched telemetry only where the documented collector is deployed. Correlate API Calls via Application Vetting / Instrumented Dynamic Analysis [Dynamic API/runtime trace: DevicePolicyManager.lockNow() or resetPassword() called by caller NOT IN $MDMAgentPackageList$]; Application Permission via Android Enterprise DPC / Application Vetting [DevicePolicyManager.getPermissionGrantState(); PackageManager manifest/requested-permission review]; Host Status via Android Enterprise DPC [DevicePolicyManager policy/compliance/security-state queries and SecurityLog events where supported]. Alert on a sequence or state change inconsistent with the device/app baseline, approved management policy, or expected user workflow; do not infer unobserved API calls, file/process activity, or payload content from management state alone.

tuning.description: MDM agent and approved Device Admin packages.

log_sources.name: mobile:DynamicAnalysis
log_sources.channel: Dynamic API/runtime trace: DevicePolicyManager.lockNow() or resetPassword() called by caller NOT IN $MDMAgentPackageList$

log_sources.channel: DevicePolicyManager policy/compliance/security-state queries and SecurityLog events where supported

analytics.name: Analytic 1696
analytics.guidance: For iOS, detect Endpoint Denial of Service from documented management, network, or vetting evidence; treat state queries as periodic observations rather than real-time events. Correlate Application Permission via Application Vetting [Code-signing entitlements and Info.plist privacy usage-description keys]; Host Status via Apple MDM [DeviceInformation / SecurityInfo / ProfileList / restrictions and compliance queries]. Alert on a sequence or state change inconsistent with the device/app baseline, approved management policy, or expected user workflow; do not infer unobserved API calls, file/process activity, or payload content from management state alone.

tuning.description: Default 300s between jailbreak detection and passcode state change.
Default 1800s sustained unreachability — distinguish from brief connectivity loss.

software.name: Xbot
software.description: [Xbot](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0298) can remotely lock infected Android devices and ask for a ransom.(Citation: PaloAlto-Xbot)

references.description: Cong Zheng, Claud Xiao and Zhi Xu. (2016, February 18). New Android Trojan “Xbot” Phishes Credit Cards and Bank Accounts, Encrypts Devices for Ransom. Retrieved December 21, 2016.

software.name: Charger
software.description: [Charger](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0323) locks the device if it is granted admin permissions, displaying a message demanding a ransom payment.(Citation: CheckPoint-Charger)

references.description: Oren Koriat and Andrey Polkovnichenko. (2017, January 24). Charger Malware Calls and Raises the Risk on Google Play. Retrieved January 24, 2017.

software.name: Exobot
software.description: [Exobot](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0522) can lock the device with a password and permanently disable the screen.(Citation: Threat Fabric Exobot)

references.description: Threat Fabric. (2017, February). Exobot - Android banking Trojan on the rise. Retrieved October 29, 2020.

software.name: GPlayed
software.description: [GPlayed](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0536) can lock the user out of the device by showing a persistent overlay.(Citation: Talos GPlayed)

references.description: V. Ventura. (2018, October 11).  GPlayed Trojan - .Net playing with Google Market . Retrieved November 24, 2020.

software.name: LightSpy
software.description: [LightSpy](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S1185) has used the DeleteSpring plugin to render the device’s user interface inoperable by disabling SpringBoard, which is iOS's home screen manager.(Citation: LinkedIn Dmitry LightSpy 2025) [LightSpy](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S1185) has used the BootDestroy plugin to prevent the victim device from booting by modifying the NVRAM parameter `auto-boot` to `false`.(Citation: LinkedIn Dmitry LightSpy 2025) Additionally, [LightSpy](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S1185) has renamed the Wi-Fi daemon to disable wireless connectivity.(Citation: LinkedIn Dmitry LightSpy 2025)

references.description: Dmitry Bestuzhev. (2025, April 7). The Coordinated Kill Switch: LightSpy's iOS Destructive Plugin Architecture Manages Device Disablement. Retrieved April 14, 2025.

mitigations.name: Use Recent OS Version
mitigations.description: Android 7 changed how the Device Administrator password APIs function.

mitigations.name: User Guidance
mitigations.description: Users should be cautioned against granting administrative access to applications.
